Both studios were placed under Ubisoft’s Creative Network division as part of a restructuring announced last year. The company emphasized its commitment to supporting affected employees, stating that RedLynx and Singapore remain integral to its global production. Separately, Ubisoft’s German studios, which employ over 600 workers across three locations, are also facing cuts, with Mainz studio responsible for the 2025 game Anno 117: Pax Romana. The layoffs follow a pattern of job reductions this year, including cuts at Massive Entertainment, Ubisoft Stockholm, and Paris headquarters. Ubisoft’s latest updates, including details about German workforce reductions, were shared via GameFile, reflecting ongoing restructuring efforts to streamline operations amid financial pressures.

item.title: Sony is taking on DJI with its new ECM-W5 wireless microphone kit
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Sony has launched the ECM-W5 wireless microphone kit, positioning it as a competitor to DJI's affordable wireless mics. Priced at $400, the kit includes two transmitters and one receiver, designed for use with Sony cameras or other devices via USB-C. It supports 32-bit float recording, capturing 96kHz audio up to 500 meters in line-of-sight conditions. The system is optimized for Sony's Alpha series cameras, connecting via the Multi Interface Shoe for power and data transfer. A single kit includes one rectangular receiver and two transmitters, but additional $120 transmitters can be purchased separately to record up to four tracks simultaneously. Each transmitter has 64GB of internal memory for backup and enables 32-bit float recording, which preserves both quiet and loud sounds without manual gain adjustments. The transmitters offer 11 hours of battery life and magnetic backplates for attaching to clothing. The receiver also includes a USB-C adapter for connecting to smartphones or PCs, and a touchscreen interface allows wireless playback via Bluetooth LE with Sony headphones. Compared to DJI's $259 Mic 3 or $99 Mic Mini, the ECM-W5's premium price may only appeal to users prioritizing 32-bit float recording for streamlined post-production. The kit is available for pre-order starting at $400, with standalone options for the $190 ECM-W5R receiver or $120 ECM-W5T transmitter for expansion. Sony emphasizes the system's flexibility for external lavalier mics, a feature beneficial for broadcasters, though its higher cost may limit its appeal compared to DJI's lower-priced alternatives.

item.title: Deezer will let listeners completely filter out AI music
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Deezer is introducing a feature that allows users to completely filter out AI-generated music from their streaming experience. The toggle, set to launch by the end of 2026, responds to growing user demand for separating human-created content from AI-generated tracks. CEO Alexis Lanternier emphasized that the feature addresses clear user preferences, stating, 'We are now giving everyone the option to remove this content completely from their streaming experience on Deezer, and focus only on human creators and creations, if they wish.' Deezer cited internal research indicating nearly half of its music streaming users would prefer AI-generated music entirely excluded from their feeds. This aligns with broader industry concerns, as NPR reported declining listener trust in AI music, with dissatisfaction worsening as platforms become saturated with such content. The company noted a significant rise in AI-generated tracks on its platform, with 18% of uploads previously classified as AI-generated, now surpassing 50%. Deezer estimates 90,000 fully AI-generated tracks are uploaded daily, accumulating to over 42 million songs. The company warns that many of these tracks are part of a 'numbers game' where creators upload hundreds of tracks in hopes one will gain traction, while also highlighting fraud risks, as up to 85% of streams from AI-generated songs are deemed fraudulent. Deezer’s AI detection tool, which it has shared with rival platforms, forms the basis for this toggle, though the system is not perfect, with the company asserting 'very low' false positive risks. Other platforms like YouTube Music and Spotify have adopted similar measures, with YouTube Music introducing labels for AI tracks and Spotify using similar labeling on AI artist pages. Deezer’s move reflects growing industry efforts to manage the proliferation of AI-generated music while balancing user preferences and content integrity.

item.title: Xbox has a teeny new gamepad
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Xbox has launched the Xbox Nano Controller, its smallest gamepad to date, priced at $50. The controller measures just over five inches in length and weighs 3.5 ounces, offering a compact design while retaining the standard Xbox controller layout. It features a rechargeable battery, an action button programmable via the Xbox Accessories app for tasks like taking screenshots or recording gameplay, and Bluetooth connectivity for compatibility with Xbox consoles, PCs, iOS, Android devices, and smart TVs. Samsung is bundling the Nano Controller with two months of Game Pass Ultimate access for new subscribers purchasing select TVs in the U.S. during the holiday season, with a similar offer planned for Meta Quest headsets. Xbox is also implementing 15-hour monthly limits on cloud gaming via Game Pass Ultimate, requiring users to purchase time credits for extended access. While the Nano Controller resembles portable gamepads from 8BitDo, it is slightly larger than the brand’s Micro controller. The controller’s triggers are noted as a potential area for improvement, as compared to the BackBone Pro and OhSnap’s MCON, which users find finicky despite their portability. Pre-orders for the Nano Controller are now open, with U.S. shipments scheduled for November 4 and global availability expanding to 35 countries by next month, with further market rollouts planned. The device aims to cater to younger players and users with smaller hands, emphasizing its ergonomic design and versatility across multiple platforms.

item.title: Ramp reaches $60B valuation as it pushes deeper into AI
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch
Expense management company Ramp announced on Thursday it has raised $1.85 billion in a new funding round, valuing the company at $60 billion. This follows a $750 million raise in June that valued Ramp at $44 billion. The latest round was co-led by Dragoneer Investment Group, Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Sands Capital, and Avenir Growth, with additional participation from over 20 other investors including Capital International, Fidelity Management & Research Company, T. Rowe Price, and Khosla Ventures. Ramp reported its annualized revenue has surpassed $2 billion, up from $1.5 billion in June, with revenue growth 25% faster than the same period last year. The company also claims annualized purchase volume exceeds $275 billion, a 175% increase from the previous year, and now serves 85,000 customers, including major clients like Visa, Uber, Shopify, Robinhood, and Figma. Ramp is expanding beyond expense management into payments, fraud detection, procurement, vendor management, and accounting, with a focus on integrating AI into its products. It launched a corporate credit card tailored for AI agents and entered the model routing business to capitalize on the AI inference market. The company also introduced Glass, a workspace for organizing AI automations and organizational knowledge. Christian Jensen of Dragoneer praised Ramp’s evolution into a broader financial operations platform with AI embedded in its operations. Ramp’s growth has positioned it in direct competition with Rippling, an HR and payroll software company that has expanded into corporate cards and expense management. Early investor Keith Rabois, who backed Ramp through Founders Fund and Khosla Ventures, stated the company is not concerned about Rippling but aims to compete with Anthropic, stating Ramp will become the primary tool for managing token spend, optimizing costs, and measuring ROI, potentially leading to a collision with Anthropic in the AI space. Ramp has now raised approximately $5 billion in total funding.

item.title: Figma announces new features to define how agents work on its platform
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch
Design platform Figma announced new features during its first Config event in India, focusing on tools to define design systems and enhance agent functionality. The company introduced Figma Specs, a Markdown-based editor allowing users to define design languages, integrate design and code libraries, and reference elements like FigJam diagrams, code layers, and canvas components. Specs can exist as standalone files or within the design canvas, serving as a centralized reference for teams and agents to adhere to brand design rules. Figma also expanded its code layers feature to open beta, enabling users to generate interactive prototypes by converting designs into code or modifying code segments. The company emphasized tools to improve AI predictability in its agent-on-canvas feature, addressing the non-deterministic nature of AI. Figma’s chief design officer, Loredana Crisan, highlighted the platform’s role in software teams, noting a 17-fold increase in code production compared to past years, though most code is used for discovery rather than shipping. The company is integrating its acquired headless CMS Payload with Figma Make to generate dynamic websites and manage content, with Payload’s downloads rising sixfold in 12 months. Figma also announced support for over 20 new tools via its MCP, including Open Code, Dia, Grok Bot, and Indian startup Sarvam. The platform opened its first India office late last year, positioning the country as its largest market outside the U.S., with 40% of India’s top 100 BSE-listed companies using Figma. These updates aim to streamline design systems, improve collaboration, and expand Figma’s capabilities for developers and designers.

item.title: Ricursive Intelligence is betting on AI-designed chips to help solve the compute crisis
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch
Ricursive Intelligence founders Anna Goldie and Azalia Mirhoseini are leveraging AI to revolutionize chip design and address the growing compute crisis. At TechCrunch Disrupt, they outlined how their startup is developing AI systems capable of designing chips, learning from iterative improvements, and accelerating the process. Goldie highlighted the urgent need for efficiency, noting that global compute demand could surge by at least 10,000 times in the next five years. She argued that building more data centers is impractical, emphasizing instead the need for more efficient chips that optimize bandwidth, wafer usage, and fabrication processes. The founders contend that AI-driven chip design allows humans to focus on innovation while machines handle execution, a shift they see happening across fields like software development. They cited AlphaChip, an AI system they previously developed, which created a circular, 'donut-shaped' chip layout that initially surprised engineers but proved effective. Unlike traditional methods that partition chips into smaller blocks, Ricursive’s approach optimizes entire chips, enabling complex patterns such as wave-like designs. This method could unlock new possibilities for custom chips in niche applications like space exploration, augmented reality, virtual reality, and biological computing. Goldie noted that reducing design time from years to weeks would make it financially viable to create specialized chips for diverse uses while improving energy efficiency. The founders also emphasized that AI’s ability to discover unconventional layouts challenges traditional design paradigms, paving the way for more efficient and versatile hardware solutions. Their work underscores a broader trend where AI enhances productivity by automating technical tasks, allowing human creativity to drive innovation in emerging technologies.

item.title: Intero Biosystems wants drugmakers to test on mini human intestines, not animals
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch
Intero Biosystems, a Denver-based startup spun out of the University of Michigan, is challenging traditional animal testing in drug development by offering human intestinal organoids as a more accurate alternative. The company’s GastroScreen product, which sells lab-grown mini intestines to pharmaceutical, biotech, food, and chemical companies, aims to reduce reliance on animal models by providing a human-relevant testing platform. Each organoid, about 1 millimeter in size, is shipped in tubes and can be used to simulate healthy tissue or disease conditions. Co-founder and CEO Charlie Childs described the organoids as "mini living organs in the mail," while co-founder and CTO Madeline Eiken emphasized their complexity, noting they contain multiple cell and tissue types found in the human intestine. Intero also provides supplies for growing the organoids and offers custom studies, including drug safety testing and disease research. For example, customers can expose the organoids to drug candidates to assess gut toxicity or test responses to compounds in disease models. Founded in 2024, the startup raised $2.3 million in a pre-seed round and generated over $400,000 in revenue from late 2023 to early 2024. Regulatory shifts, including the FDA’s push to reduce animal testing and its draft guidance on validating non-animal methods, have spurred interest in alternatives like organoids. Intero differentiates itself by using induced pluripotent stem cells derived from blood samples, enabling scalable, personalized models. While still in the second stage of a three-part validation process, the company has shown GastroScreen’s ability to predict responses to drugs that reduce intestinal inflammation or damage the gut. Long-term goals include scaling production to hundreds of thousands of organoids per batch and advancing into personalized medicine, with an ultimate vision of creating an artificial intestine. Intero also plans to license biological data generated from its organoids to AI companies. The startup is currently competing in TechCrunch Disrupt’s Startup Battlefield, highlighting its role in the growing field of human-relevant drug testing alternatives.

item.title: Ambani’s Jio seeks to raise $3.2B in what could be India’s biggest IPO
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch
Jio Platforms, the digital arm of Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries, is seeking to raise up to $3.2 billion in what could become India’s largest initial public offering (IPO). The offering, which opens for subscription on October 21 and closes on October 23, sets a price band of ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 ($11.19 to $11.76) per share for up to 270 million new shares. At the upper end of the price band, the IPO could value Jio at ₹10.3 trillion ($108.3 billion), surpassing the ₹4.91 trillion ($65 billion) valuation from 2020 when Meta and Google invested $5.7 billion and $4.5 billion respectively. The IPO would overtake Hyundai Motor India’s 2024 offering of ₹278.7 billion ($3.3 billion) even at the lower end of the price range. Jio, launched in 2016, has grown to India’s largest telecom operator with over 524 million subscribers, expanding beyond telecom into broadband, cloud services, and digital businesses. Its recent financials show revenue of ₹391.7 billion ($4.1 billion) and net profit of ₹77.6 billion ($816 million) for the quarter ended June, per its IPO prospectus. Jio plans to allocate up to ₹275 billion ($2.9 billion) from the IPO to repay debt at its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm, with remaining funds for general corporate purposes. The IPO also reserves ₹25 billion ($263 million) for eligible Reliance Industries shareholders and ₹5 billion ($53 million) for employees at a discounted rate. The offering comes amid Elon Musk’s criticism of Ambani over alleged efforts to block Starlink in India, though Indian authorities have rejected Musk’s claims. Jio’s IPO marks a significant step in its expansion, reflecting its growth from a telecom provider to a diversified digital services company.

item.title: Flock CEO says its microphones detect ‘just gunshots’ — its website says different
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch
Flock CEO Garrett Langley claims the company’s gunshot-detection microphones are designed to detect only gunshots, but Flock’s website describes the technology as capable of identifying a broader range of sounds, including car crashes, fireworks, and disruptive community events. During an onstage interview at TechCrunch Disrupt, Langley defended the product, arguing that critics misunderstand its capabilities. He emphasized that the system’s primary purpose is to provide earlier awareness of potential public safety events, such as gunfire, by notifying users when a gunshot occurs. However, the company’s website states that its audio systems can also detect street takeovers, severe crashes, and other ambient sounds to enhance situational awareness. This discrepancy has drawn criticism, particularly after Flock initially announced the technology could listen for ‘sounds of human distress’ and ‘screaming,’ prompting backlash from privacy groups. The company later revised its messaging to avoid implying it monitors conversations or analyzes speech, and eventually removed the distress-detection feature from customer systems. Langley acknowledged that some customers requested alerts for non-gunshot events, like abductions, leading to a prototype that faced concerns. He insisted the product is ‘just gunshots’ and that the website’s broader descriptions were misleading. A Flock spokesperson clarified that while the technology can detect additional sounds, it is not designed to monitor conversations or analyze speech. The website’s FAQ section notes that the detection library expands to include emerging threats relevant to customers’ needs. Langley also compared Flock’s microphone count to ShotSpotter’s 25,000 units as of 2024. The controversy comes amid growing public scrutiny of Flock, including protests in San Francisco and the termination of partnerships with Texas, Florida, and Amazon’s Ring. Privacy advocates, including the ACLU, have criticized the company’s surveillance practices, with some individuals even destroying its cameras. Langley’s comments highlight ongoing tensions between Flock’s claims about its technology’s scope and the concerns of critics and users.

item.title: Electric vehicle sales in the US are showing signs of life
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch
Electric vehicle sales in the U.S. are rebounding after a decline following the cancellation of federal tax credits last year. A new report from Cox Automotive reveals that EV sales have grown for three consecutive quarters, with EVs capturing 6.1% of the U.S. market—the highest share since the third quarter of 2025. Stephanie Valdez Streaty, director of industry insights at Cox Automotive, noted that the market is 'finding its footing again,' attributing the recovery to more competitive EV pricing and rising gas prices. Toyota, Rivian, and Subaru led the growth, with Toyota’s bZ and Lexus RZ models seeing sales double after a refresh that included Tesla-style charging ports, larger batteries, more powerful motors, and faster charging times. Tesla, despite a 20% year-over-year sales drop, still holds the largest share, accounting for over half of all EV sales in the third quarter. The U.S. recovery mirrors Germany’s experience after its government abruptly ended EV purchase incentives in November 2023, causing a sharp sales decline. However, the German market rebounded, with EV sales in August 2024 reaching the second-highest level on record. The report suggests that despite initial setbacks, EV adoption in both countries is stabilizing and gaining momentum, driven by affordability and external factors like fuel costs.

item.title: Your dusty Nest and Home speakers just got a surprise firmware lifeline
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Google is rolling out a firmware update for older Nest and Home speakers, targeting devices like the original Google Home, Home Mini, Nest Mini, and Nest Audio. The update, version 3.79.550760, is currently in testing via the Home Preview Program and is expected to be released more broadly in the coming weeks, though no specific date has been announced. The Google Home Max is excluded from this update. The update aims to enhance the smart home experience by improving voice command functionality and device integration, ensuring older speakers remain useful despite their age. These devices, released between 2016 and 2020, can still handle basic tasks like playing audio and managing smart home functions, but their software has not received the same attention as newer models. While the update may improve reliability and convenience, it is unlikely to replace newer hardware or introduce major new features. Users can access the update through the Google Home app by enrolling in the Preview Program, where the firmware will install automatically. Additionally, a separate October update will enhance Gemini’s capabilities for Home conversations, voice commands, weather responses, and device controls. Google’s efforts highlight its commitment to maintaining functionality for older devices, offering users an alternative to replacing them with newer models.

item.title: Samsung Health update is all treats: Sleep and Running Coaches get needed changes
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Samsung announced an October update for its Health app, focusing on improvements to the Sleep and Running Coaches. The Sleep Coach now requires only three days of sleep data from the past two weeks, down from seven days in a month, to generate weekly guidance. Users must complete a survey about sleep regularity, interruptions, and caffeine intake to create a tailored four- to eight-week coaching program. A new Sleep Balance graph will display metrics like sleep time, regularity, awake time, satisfaction, and Energy Score, while morning insights provide personalized tips based on sleep trends. The Running Coach’s training levels have been expanded from 10 to 12 tiers to accommodate intermediate and advanced runners, allowing them to set higher performance benchmarks. Samsung also enhanced its partnership with Strava, enabling users to import running and cycling routes into the Health app. These updates aim to simplify weekly guidance and improve user engagement. Additionally, the app’s Energy Score has been revamped with AI, and the Vitals feature—introduced before the Galaxy Watch 9 launch—tracks heart metrics like heart rate, variability, respiratory rate, skin temperature, and blood oxygen, offering insights for medical consultations. The changes are part of Samsung’s ongoing efforts to refine its Health app for better user health tracking and personalized coaching.

item.title: More Nothing smart glasses rumors suggest we might see two variations
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Rumors circulating on social media platforms like Bluesky suggest that Nothing, the company known for its Android phones, headphones, and earbuds, is developing two variations of smart glasses. Tipster Roland Quandt claims the brand is working on a pair of smart glasses with two distinct versions: one equipped with a camera and another without. The 'audio-equipped' model is said to allow users to place and receive calls, featuring auto-tinting photochromic lenses that darken outdoors and clear indoors. These glasses would integrate closely with the user's phone's AI assistant. The camera version, meanwhile, could offer similar functionalities as the audio model but may also include translation capabilities and access to ChatGPT. However, details about the camera-equipped variant remain sparse. Earlier this year, rumors indicated that Nothing CEO Carl Pei had shifted the company's focus toward AI-powered smart glasses, with a potential 2027 release. The project reportedly involves a camera, speaker, and microphone, though some aspects might be separated into distinct features. Unlike previous speculation, the latest rumors suggest the glasses may rely heavily on the phone for processing tasks, such as cloud-based AI computations. Privacy concerns surrounding cameras on smart glasses, akin to the backlash faced by Meta's similar devices, have been highlighted. The article also speculates on the design of the glasses, noting that Nothing's aesthetic has drawn attention, and questions whether the company might adopt a transparent design or align with the styling of its upcoming phones. While these rumors remain unconfirmed, they reflect ongoing interest in Nothing's potential expansion into wearable technology.

item.title: Android 17 could soon fix your phone's Wi-Fi and mobile data problems for you
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Google is developing new diagnostic tools in Android 17 to help users troubleshoot and resolve issues with Wi-Fi, mobile data, and call connectivity. These tools, part of the Device Health & Support section, will allow Pixel phones to identify underlying problems with network connections, calls, or data services. If an issue is detected, the system may attempt an automatic fix or guide users through manual troubleshooting steps, eliminating the need for manual configuration or repeated resets. The functionality was spotted in the Android 17 QPR3 Beta 1 release and the latest Google Play Services beta, though it is not yet available to the general public. While the tools are currently in testing, there is speculation they could be included in the stable Android 17 QPR3 update early next year. Connectivity problems on Android devices, particularly with Wi-Fi and mobile data, have been a recurring concern for Pixel users, and these built-in diagnostics aim to address that by providing proactive solutions. The addition of call-related diagnostics expands on existing tools for battery health, Bluetooth, and touchscreen issues, further enhancing the device’s self-troubleshooting capabilities. Users experiencing dropped calls, intermittent Wi-Fi, or sudden data disconnections may benefit from the automated assistance these tools offer, potentially reducing the time and effort required to resolve such issues. Google’s ongoing efforts to improve diagnostic features reflect a broader trend of integrating more intelligent troubleshooting into its ecosystem, aiming to enhance user experience by minimizing manual intervention.

item.title: Google's next TV Streamer sounds like a massive upgrade — Apple should be worried
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Google is reportedly developing a next-generation TV Streamer that could introduce significant upgrades over its current model. The new device is expected to maintain a similar overall design but feature a slightly narrower profile for a more compact form factor. Key enhancements include built-in far-field microphones, which would allow users to interact with Gemini hands-free by simply saying 'Hey Google' without needing to pick up the remote. The report also mentions a presence-sensing feature, similar to some TCL smart TVs, which could automatically detect when someone enters the room and trigger actions like displaying the time, weather, or a Google Photos screensaver. Hardware improvements are anticipated, such as a faster processor, increased storage capacity beyond the current 32GB, and a redesigned remote with additional shortcut buttons for YouTube and Netflix. The new remote may also include a dedicated 'Find My Remote' button. While the report does not specify a launch date or pricing, it notes that Apple is preparing to unveil a new Apple TV 4K, suggesting Google might announce its upgraded streaming device later this fall. The article emphasizes that the current Google TV Streamer remains a strong option despite a recent $50 price increase, but the upcoming changes could further solidify its position in the market. Details about the new model will be updated as more information becomes available.

item.title: Users find a weird issue with the Kindle 2026: Amazon says it was 'expected'
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Early users of the 2026 Amazon Kindle line are reporting a 'light bleed' issue in dark mode, where bright glows appear along the edges of the device. The problem is most noticeable when reading with high brightness settings in dark mode, causing a glow that mirrors white text against the black background. Amazon acknowledged the issue in a statement, calling it 'expected' as part of achieving a 'color bezel' design. The company advised users to lower brightness in dark mode to reduce the effect. Users on platforms like Reddit have shared photos and complaints, noting that older models like the Paperwhite 2024 did not exhibit this problem. Some users argue the issue is abnormal, while others have not noticed it. Amazon did not confirm whether replacements are available but suggested contacting customer support. The 2026 Kindle lineup includes models like the $150 six-inch Kindle with 16GB storage, six weeks of battery life, and faster book-opening speeds. The $200 Paperwhite and $250 Signature Edition are also available, alongside a new Bluetooth page-turner remote called the Kindle Click. While some models are available for immediate shipping, the Paperwhite and Colorsoft versions require pre-orders. Amazon emphasized the redesigned display, which features a reverse-stack design to make the device lighter and thinner, though the light bleed issue has sparked user frustration.

item.title: Samsung could soon challenge Apple, Sony, and Bose with its Galaxy Studio headphones
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Samsung is reportedly developing its first Galaxy-branded over-ear headphones, which could be launched under the Galaxy Studio name. The leak, shared by leaker evowizz on X, follows their previous accurate revelations about Samsung’s Galaxy Buds On earbuds. While no official confirmation has been made, the rumored product could debut as early as November, potentially during a Galaxy Glasses event the company is preparing for. The Galaxy Studio headphones aim to compete with premium offerings from Apple, Sony, Bose, and Sennheiser, which have dominated the over-ear headphone market. Details about the design, features, and pricing remain undisclosed, though the leak suggests Samsung plans to position the headphones as a direct rival to models like Apple’s AirPods Max and Sony’s WH-1000X series. The leak comes amid Samsung’s broader strategy to expand its audio product lineup, which already includes the Galaxy Buds series. However, the company has not yet confirmed the launch date or specifications for the Galaxy Studio headphones. The revelation has generated anticipation, as Samsung seeks to challenge established competitors in the premium headphone space. Further details are expected to emerge as the company approaches its November product rollout, though no official announcement has been made at this time.

item.title: The Amazon Alexa Tablet series runs Android, and turns into a 'sanctuary' for Kindle readers
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Amazon announced its new Alexa Tablet series on October 8, introducing three models: the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, Tablet 11, and Tablet 8. The 12 Pro, the flagship model, features a 12-inch display with two variants—vibrant and Nanomatte—designed for outdoor use with anti-glare technology. It includes a 4nm 8-core chip, quad Dolby Atmos speakers, and multitasking capabilities via a stylus and keyboard. Priced at $499 for the vibrant display and $549 for the Nanomatte variant, the 12 Pro also integrates Alexa Plus for voice commands, smart home controls, and On-Screen Intelligence for enhanced interactions. The device transforms into a 'distraction-free reading sanctuary' via the Kindle app, silencing notifications and reducing blue light for extended reading sessions. Accessories include the Tablet Pro Pen and Keyboard. The Tablet 11, with an 11-inch display, focuses on entertainment with a 90Hz refresh rate, 16:10 cinematic aspect ratio, and dual Dolby Atmos speakers, priced at $329.99. The Tablet 8, an 8-inch model, targets e-readers with a 14-hour video playback battery and $229.99 price. All tablets share a 6.5mm aluminum body, with the 12 Pro offering up to 20 hours of battery life. Amazon also launched Kids Tablets in 8.7-inch and 11-inch sizes, available today but shipping to the U.S., Mexico, and Canada on October 14. The 12 Pro’s Nanomatte display, developed with Corning, maintains sharpness while reducing glare, and the series emphasizes Alexa integration for daily tasks and media consumption.

item.title: Samsung is reportedly cutting smartphone production as memory costs soar
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Samsung is reportedly cutting smartphone production as rising memory chip costs threaten its profitability. According to a report by Korean outlet Money Today, the company has asked suppliers to reduce Q4 smartphone production by 20% to 30%, which could lower its 2026 total output from an expected 270 million units to around 200 million. The decision stems from a sharp increase in DRAM prices, which are squeezing margins and making it difficult to sell certain models profitably. Manufacturers face a dilemma: absorb higher component costs and reduce profits per device or pass on price hikes that could deter buyers. Samsung’s strategy shift involves focusing less on low-margin models and prioritizing its premium Galaxy lineup, potentially leading to fewer budget options and higher prices for consumers. The production cuts also come amid a seasonal slowdown as buyers await the next Galaxy S series, though the reported reduction is significantly larger than typical seasonal adjustments. In 2025, Samsung produced approximately 240 million smartphones, matching Apple’s volume as the world’s largest smartphone maker by unit count. However, the company’s ability to maintain this scale is now under pressure from escalating memory chip costs. TrendForce estimates highlight the industry’s reliance on DRAM, which has become a critical factor in profitability. Samsung has not officially confirmed the production cuts, leaving uncertainty about whether this represents a temporary adjustment or a long-term strategic shift. The situation underscores the challenges faced by smartphone manufacturers in balancing rising input costs with competitive pricing and consumer demand.

item.title: Ultrahuman's Heart Scan for Ring PRO needs only sixty seconds for crucial insights
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Ultrahuman has launched the 'Heart Scan' feature for its Ring PRO users, offering a 60-second on-demand heart check-in to provide real-time insights into cardiovascular health. The feature, available through the Ultrahuman app, captures a snapshot of the user's heart activity and generates a downloadable report with details such as pulse recordings, tachograms, and Lorenz plots of beat-to-beat timing. Ring PRO members can access the report via the Ultrahuman Dashboard. The scan aims to help users understand how their heart responds to different activities, such as exercise, relaxation, or stress, by analyzing metrics like heart rate variability (HRV), resting heart rate, and overnight recovery. The Heart Scan integrates with the Cardio Adaptability PowerPlug, which tracks long-term heart trends, complementing the scan's focus on immediate moments. The feature is rolling out in the U.S. on October 7, with eligible Ring PRO members able to enable free scans. Ultrahuman also announced the HealthEx PowerPlug, a $4.99/month or $45.99/year subscription service that syncs users' medical records from U.S. healthcare facilities with Ring PRO data. This service can generate 'Visit Packs' for doctor's appointments, combining medical records with biometric data to enhance healthcare interactions. The company, which has raised $70 million in funding from investors including Qualcomm Ventures and Labcorp, aims to develop platforms that interpret human biology to empower health decisions. The updates reflect Ultrahuman's broader vision of leveraging health technology to improve personal well-being through actionable insights.

item.title: The Xiaomi 18 Ultra would've had insane cameras, but it looks like we'll never get it
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Rumors circulating on X and Weibo suggest the Xiaomi 18 Ultra has been canceled, with its high price likely being the reason. A tipster on Weibo claims the device would have featured a triple 200MP LOFIC camera setup, including a 200MP main lens on a 1/1.12-inch sensor, a 200MP ultra-wide lens on a 1/1.56-inch sensor, and a 200MP periscope telephoto lens with optical zoom. The phone was also rumored to have a flat display with 1mm bezels. Tipster Abhishek Yadav on X confirmed the cancellation, stating the phone's price—estimated at 9,999 RMB (~$1,499)—may have led to the decision. While the 18 Ultra’s specs were reportedly similar to the 18 Pro and Pro Max models, which debuted in mid-September 2024, the Ultra would have included a 200MP ultra-wide camera absent from the Pro variants. The 18 Pro Max features a 200MP main lens and a 200MP periscope telephoto sensor, while the 18 Pro adds a 50MP ultra-wide camera. Despite the cancellation, Yadav noted an Ultra model could return in Xiaomi’s 19 series. The 18 Pro and Pro Max have been praised for their camera performance, with the 17 Ultra’s telephoto lens previously highlighted as a standout. Analysts suggest Xiaomi may revisit the Ultra lineup in 2027, potentially leveraging advanced camera technology while balancing cost considerations.

item.title: Qualcomm and Arm are back in court, and your next phone is on the line
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Qualcomm and Arm are engaged in a five-day jury trial in a Delaware federal court, with the case centering on Qualcomm’s 2021 acquisition of chip startup Nuvia and subsequent contractual disputes. Qualcomm alleges Arm violated its contract by withholding mandatory chip-testing tools required for Nuvia’s operations and leaking threats to end a key license in 2024, which allegedly harmed Qualcomm’s negotiations with Meta. The company claims the leak reduced the value of its Meta deal by $170 million, though Arm denies the link, attributing changes in the deal to Meta’s shift from virtual reality headsets to AI glasses. Qualcomm is seeking to halt royalty payments to Arm for up to five years, a move that could cost the chipmaker billions in royalties, as Qualcomm’s 2026 revenue from Arm accounts for about 9% of its total. Judge Maryellen Noreika is evaluating whether the five-year royalty suspension should stand, which could significantly impact Qualcomm’s financials. The dispute also includes a secondary bench trial assessing whether Arm negotiated its next-generation architecture in good faith, with both companies currently bound by a contract through 2033. The trial’s outcome could reshape how Arm and major chipmakers negotiate future CPU technology licensing and control, with broader implications for the smartphone industry. Qualcomm asserts Arm undercut its business post-Nuvia acquisition, while Arm calls the lawsuit leverage in a business dispute, arguing Qualcomm cannot prove damages. The case highlights high-stakes tensions over intellectual property, licensing terms, and the competitive landscape of semiconductor technology.

item.title: Googlebooks are here, but Google says some laptops might struggle with app support
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Google has launched its Googlebook line of laptops, but the company has clarified that not all models will support full Android app functionality. The devices, available for pre-order since September 21 and officially launched on October 4 (U.S.) and October 5 (U.K. and other regions), come with varying processor types. Google warns that laptops using Intel Core Ultra 5 processors—specifically models from Acer, ASUS, and Lenovo—may struggle to run certain Android apps from the Play Store. This is because most Android apps are optimized for ARM-based chips, which are standard in smartphones, while Intel processors require additional developer adjustments for compatibility. Qualcomm-powered models from HP and Dell, however, are expected to support full Play Store functionality without issues. Google acknowledges that a 'small handful of complex apps or games' may need tuning to run optimally on Intel-based devices but assures that 'the vast majority of Android apps run smoothly' on both Intel and Qualcomm platforms. The company is collaborating with developers, Intel, and Qualcomm to address the compatibility challenges. Critics argue the limitation should have been disclosed upfront, as users might encounter unexpected app failures or glitches. The Googlebook line includes features like touchscreens, haptic glass trackpads, backlit keyboards, and strong Android phone integration. item.title: Chrome for Android might soon force a biometric scan before filling your passwords
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Google is testing a new security feature for Chrome on Android that would require biometric authentication, such as fingerprint or face scan, before autofilling saved passwords. The feature, previously tested over a year ago but removed before reaching the stable release, has been reintroduced in the latest Chrome Canary build. A "Biometric reauth for password filling" flag was added, allowing users to enable the setting, which would prompt authentication before Chrome auto-fills stored credentials. This change aims to prevent unauthorized access to password vaults if a device is unlocked, as simply unlocking the phone would no longer suffice. The extra verification step addresses a security gap in Google Password Manager, where biometric checks for password autofill were already available in other apps but not in Chrome’s browser. Unlike Apple’s Safari, which uses biometric authentication for password autofill on iPhones via Face ID or Touch ID, Google’s proposed feature would integrate this reauthentication specifically when accessing saved passwords in Chrome. The update is currently in the Canary testing phase, with no stable release date announced. If implemented, the change would enhance security by ensuring only the device owner can access saved passwords, though it remains a testing option for now. The feature’s return to Canary suggests Google is actively refining it, though the exact timeline for a full rollout remains unclear.
